name: MMseqs2, three rounds
kind: builds a profile of a protein family
compares: A profile of a protein family, built by MMseqs2 from its own hits over three rounds of search, as jackhmmer does.
reference: The relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as an MMseqs2 database.
score: Bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
caveats: At most 1,000 target proteins are kept per query (--max-seqs 1000). How often that cut hits: not measured.
Each round can pull in proteins from a different family. How often: not measured.

known_failure_modes.finding: A call is the whole alignment, not the target's domain placed on the query, so a long alignment over repeats never lands on one repeat. On a 23-aa LRR_1 repeat, every MMseqs2 and phmmer call was 47 aa or longer, so none landed.
known_failure_modes.number: 47 aa or longer, on a 23-aa repeat

evidence.quote: But every one of their calls is 47 aa or longer, so under half of it lies inside a 23-aa repeat, and the landing rule (at least half the call inside the domain) rejects it.
a call is the whole alignment, not the target's domain projected onto the query, so long alignments over repeats never land on one repeat.
Olga's decision (2026-10-14, before the test half was read): a call is the target domain placed on the query through the hit, and MMseqs2 runs one round (2067fa1; recorded in nb 280's first cell).

known_failure_modes.run: the time-split pilot's tune half (notebook 280), rapeseed protein A0A078HBQ0, LRR_1 repeats 64-86 and 88-110
known_failure_modes.what_to_do: Place the target's domain on the query through the alignment before scoring. Notebook 280 switched to this rule; the leaderboard's own calls are still whole alignments.

known_failure_modes.finding: Aligner calls run past the domain, because a call spans the whole aligned stretch. Over correct calls, they start a median 5 to 21 residues early. Over all calls, 45% to 60% start more than 100 residues early.
known_failure_modes.number: median 5 to 21 residues early; 45% to 60% more than 100 residues early

evidence.quote: Over correct calls, the median of call start minus true start is 0 for hmmscan, whose models define the Pfam truth, so the 1-based reading of truth and aligners holds. Aligners start a median 5 to 21 residues early, because a call spans the whole aligned stretch.
45% to 60% of aligner calls start more than 100 residues early, not "most"

known_failure_modes.run: `make leaderboard-pileup` and the region pile-up page (Figure 4)
known_failure_modes.what_to_do: Read a call's ends as the alignment's ends, not the domain's. To score where a domain sits, place the target's domain through the alignment.

known_failure_modes.finding: Three rounds of profile search gave dipeptide-shuffled decoy proteins hits as strong as E 1e-22. One round gave them none below E 0.026. So with three rounds, a cutoff matched to decoys is set by the profile's own drift toward a family.

evidence.quote: The 3-round profile search gave dipeptide-shuffled decoys hits down to E 1e-22, and one round gives none below E 0.026.

known_failure_modes.run: `make mmseqs-one-round`, Slurm job 47690191, on the time-split pilot's tune half; tables in `pilot_partial_2026-10-13/mmseqs_one_round/`
known_failure_modes.what_to_do: Run one round (`--num-iterations 1`) when a cutoff is matched to decoys, or set the cutoff separately for each number of rounds.

command:
mmseqs search \
    human-38fdd87d_mmdb/db zebrafish_mmdb/db result mmseqs_tmp \
    --threads 16 \
    -s 7 \
    --num-iterations 3 \
    --max-seqs 1000 \
    -e 10.0
questions: Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.241 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.300 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.337 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.209 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, setting sensitivity 7, 3 rounds; subsets with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.245 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.319 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.462 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.028 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.085 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, setting sensitivity 7, 3 rounds.)
Can you spend about 0.0787 core-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured mean per relative; see "Cost per 1,000 queries" below.
